dbinternals.title: Database Internals
dbinternals.description: Look inside a database engine: storage, indexes, query optimization, logging and recovery, and concurrency control.
dbinternals.audience: For engineers who use databases daily and want to understand how they work and why queries behave as they do.
dbinternals.goal: Explain and build the core components of a database storage engine.

relatedTracks.reason: Using SQL, modeling, and operating databases
Caches and memory behavior that shape storage design

levels.goal: Understand how data is laid out on disk and in memory.

skills.name: Storage, Pages & Buffer Pools
skills.description: Learn how records are stored in pages and how a buffer pool caches them.
outcomes: Describe heap files, slotted pages, and row versus column layout
Explain buffer pool replacement policies
Estimate the I/O cost of a table scan

resources.label: YouTube search: database storage pages and buffer pool

skills.name: B-Trees & B+Trees
skills.description: Understand the index structure behind most relational databases.
outcomes: Insert and split nodes in a B+Tree by hand
Explain why B+Trees suit disk-based storage
Analyze range-scan and point-lookup cost

resources.label: Use The Index, Luke: SQL indexing guide
YouTube search: B+ tree explained for databases

project.title: Disk-backed key-value store
project.description: Build a page-based key-value store with a buffer pool and a B+Tree index, and benchmark point and range reads.

levels.goal: Compare write-optimized structures and understand how queries are planned.

skills.name: LSM Trees & Write-Optimized Storage
skills.description: Study memtables, SSTables, compaction, and Bloom filters.
outcomes: Explain the LSM write and read path
Compare compaction strategies and write amplification
Choose between B-Tree and LSM engines for a workload

resources.label: Designing Data-Intensive Applications: Storage and retrieval
YouTube search: LSM tree explained compaction

skills.name: Query Processing & Optimization
skills.description: See how SQL becomes a plan, and how the optimizer chooses join order and access paths.
outcomes: Read an EXPLAIN ANALYZE plan
Explain nested-loop, hash, and merge joins
Describe cost models, statistics, and cardinality estimation

resources.label: Use The Index, Luke: Join operations
YouTube search: how query optimizers work join ordering

project.title: Storage engine comparison
project.description: Add an LSM engine next to your B+Tree store, compare write and read performance, and explain the plans of five queries on a real database.

levels.goal: Provide durability and isolation under concurrency.

skills.name: Write-Ahead Logging & Crash Recovery
skills.description: Guarantee durability with logging, checkpoints, and the ARIES recovery algorithm.
outcomes: Explain write-ahead logging and group commit
Describe the analysis, redo, and undo phases of ARIES
Test recovery by killing a process mid-write

resources.label: SQLite: How SQLite implements atomic commit
Wikipedia: Algorithms for Recovery and Isolation Exploiting Semantics
YouTube search: ARIES recovery algorithm explained

skills.name: Concurrency Control & MVCC
skills.description: Compare locking, timestamp ordering, and multi-version concurrency control.
outcomes: Explain snapshot isolation and write skew
Compare two-phase locking and MVCC
Reproduce an isolation anomaly in a real database

resources.label: PostgreSQL Docs: Concurrency control and MVCC
A Critique of ANSI SQL Isolation Levels (paper)
YouTube search: MVCC and snapshot isolation explained

project.title: Crash-safe transactional store
project.description: Add a write-ahead log and snapshot reads to your store, then test crash recovery and concurrent transactions.

capstone.title: Build a small database engine
capstone.description: Combine storage, indexes, a query executor, logging, and transactions into a small database and document the design trade-offs.

hci.title: Human-Computer Interaction

hci.audience: For developers and designers who want a scientific basis for interface decisions.

ir.title: Information Retrieval & Search
ir.description: Learn how search systems index, rank, evaluate, and serve results, from inverted indexes to hybrid vector search.
ir.audience: For engineers building search, recommendation, or retrieval-augmented applications.
ir.goal: Build and evaluate a search system with measurable relevance.

levels.goal: Build an index and rank documents by relevance.

skills.description: Tokenize, normalize, and index text so queries can be answered quickly.
outcomes: Build an inverted index with postings lists
Apply tokenization, stemming, and stop-word handling
Answer boolean and phrase queries

Stanford CS276: Information Retrieval and Web Search
